html:
The Mau was a non-violent movement for Samoan self-rule, first against German rule and then, from the 1920s, against New Zealand. Its members wore a uniform of purple lavalava and refused to cooperate with the administration.

Anger grew after the 1918 influenza, which New Zealand let ashore and which killed about a fifth of the people. On 28 December 1929, Black Saturday, New Zealand police fired on a Mau procession in Apia and killed its leader, Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III, and others.

The Mau women's wing kept it going while men were in hiding. Its demands were met with independence in 1962.
